title: Finite abelian-group decomposition

problem.name: Finite abelian-group decomposition
problem.statement_latex: Given generators and uniquely encoded reversible group operations for a finite abelian group $G$, output elements $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ and orders $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ with $G=\langle g_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langle g_r\rangle$ and $|g_i|=d_i$. Let $n$ bound the encoding length and $\log_2|G|$.
problem.statement_text: Given generators and uniquely encoded reversible group operations for a finite abelian group $G$, output elements $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ and orders $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ with $G=\langle g_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langle g_r\rangle$ and $|g_i|=d_i$. Let $n$ bound the encoding length and $\log_2|G|$.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The Luo--Li--Le Gall implementation uses $O(n)$ logical qubits and $\widetilde O(n^{5/2}T_{\rm op})$ total quantum gates, with the circuit repetitions specified above.
hardware.description_text: The Luo–Li–Le Gall implementation uses $O(n)$ logical qubits and $\widetilde O(n^{5/2}T_{\rm op})$ total quantum gates, with the circuit repetitions specified above.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time by Cheung--Mosca. Luo--Li--Le Gall improve the implementation: for operation cost $T_{\rm op}=\Omega(\sqrt n)$, at most $O(\sqrt n)$ distinct circuits of size $\widetilde O(nT_{\rm op})$, each repeated $O(n)$ times, with $O(n)$ qubits and polynomial classical postprocessing.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time by Cheung–Mosca. Luo–Li–Le Gall improve the implementation: for operation cost $T_{\rm op}=\Omega(\sqrt n)$, at most $O(\sqrt n)$ distinct circuits of size $\widetilde O(nT_{\rm op})$, each repeated $O(n)$ times, with $O(n)$ qubits and polynomial classical postprocessing.

classical.headline_latex: $O(|G|^{1/2})$ generic group operations by Sutherland's Monte Carlo structure algorithm, with representation-dependent bit costs. Groups supplied with an explicit decomposition admit faster classical processing.
classical.headline_text: $O(|G|^{1/2})$ generic group operations by Sutherland's Monte Carlo structure algorithm, with representation-dependent bit costs. Groups supplied with an explicit decomposition admit faster classical processing.
